body:
I reported several figures about the annotation store during the 2026-08-18
reconnaissance and repeated two of them to the operator. Re-measuring on
2026-08-19 they do not reproduce. Recording the correction here because the
wrong numbers are in a merged finding (F-7e418c) and in the session record, and
one of them was used to argue that a risk was small.

## What I can measure today

`local-dev/config/app.db` is the database the dev server serves — `cwn-local`
mounts it at `/config` (OBSERVED via `docker inspect`). It holds:

    632 annotations across 19 books
    webreader   621   (566 carry cfi_range)
    koreader      8   (0 carry cfi_range)
    kobo          3   (2 carry cfi_range)

    annotation columns: ... cfi_range, source, hidden, position_type ...
    there is NO annotation_type column at all

Newest row is 2026-08-15, so nothing was written by this session's test runs;
this is not test pollution.

## What I reported, and what is wrong with it

1. "628 annotations / 11 books — 624 kobo, 4 webreader."
   Wrong, and close to inverted on source. It is 632 / 19, and 621 are
   webreader while 3 are kobo.

2. "615 of 628 rows have annotation_type NULL; 10 dogear, 3 highlight."
   Not reproducible. The column does not exist in this database, so no
   distribution over it can be measured. `_ensure_kobo_two_way_gate_columns`
   (cps/ub.py) adds it at server start, so a server running current code against
   this config would create it — and every existing row would then be NULL,
   which is the shape of the original claim. But "615 of 628" is a specific
   count I cannot substantiate.

3. "Only 4 of 628 annotations have cfi_range." **This is the one that mattered.**
   The real figure is 566 of 621 webreader rows, plus 2 kobo — three orders of
   magnitude off. I used the small number to tell the operator that the
   web-reader CFI exposure from splitting spine documents was negligible. It is
   not negligible; it is the majority of the store.

## Most likely cause, and why it is not a good excuse

`cwn-mine` mounted `/tmp/cwnmine.pInRLt/config` (OBSERVED via `docker inspect`)
— a throwaway container with its OWN config directory, now gone with /tmp. If
the figures came from there they described a disposable test database while
being reported as "the live server". I did not record which database I queried,
which is the actual defect: a measurement without its source is not a
measurement, and this one travelled into a merged finding and into a risk
argument.

## What still stands, because it was verified in code and not by counting

F-7e418c's CODE claims are unaffected and re-verified 2026-08-19:

  * `cps/services/kobo_import.py` — `ParsedBookmark` has no type field, the
    Bookmark SELECT does not read `Type`, and the row built at ~line 324 cannot
    populate `annotation_type`. The importer genuinely never sets it.
  * `cps/services/annotation_sync/__init__.py:312` — the live path sets it only
    `if "type" in payload`, so a PATCH omitting `type` leaves it NULL.
  * The importer's SELECT is `WHERE Text IS NOT NULL AND Text != ''`, so dogears
    never reach it at all — which makes any claim about imported dogear rows
    suspect on its face.

## Consequence already acted on

The cfi_range correction is why the split guard added on 2026-08-19 matters more
than I argued for it: `upload_book_formats` and `TaskConvert` now refuse to split
a book that has ANY annotation, so a book carrying cfi_range anchors is never
re-spined underneath the web reader.

## Rule for next time

Record the database path beside any figure taken from one, and re-run the query
before quoting the figure in an argument. A number with no reproducible source
should be written as an impression, not as a measurement.
title: Correction: my annotation-store measurements from 2026-08-18 do not reproduce
